lessons.title: What molecular dynamics is
lessons.summary: Simulating how atoms move, step by step, and the files GROMACS uses.

blocks.text: Structure prediction gives you one static picture. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulates motion: it computes the force on every atom from a force field (a set of equations and parameters for bonds, angles, charges and contacts), moves each atom a tiny step (2 femtoseconds), and repeats millions of times. Watching a designed protein in water for 100 nanoseconds shows whether it stays folded, whether a binding loop flops around, and more.
GROMACS is a fast, widely used MD program. Everything goes through one command, `gmx`, followed by a subcommand: `gmx pdb2gmx`, `gmx solvate`, `gmx mdrun`, and so on. On Geiss-01 it's a module.

flags: Where each atom is (.gro is GROMACS's own format)
What the molecules are: atoms, bonds, charges, and how many of each
Settings for a step: how long, what temperature, which algorithms
Coordinates + topology + parameters in one binary file, made by grompp, run by mdrun
Energies over time, and the run's log
The atoms' positions over time: the movie
Saved state, to continue a run that stopped

quiz.q: Which file does `gmx mdrun` actually run?
quiz.why: grompp combines coordinates, topology and parameters into a .tpr, and mdrun runs that.

lessons.title: Building the system
lessons.summary: Topology, box, water and ions: the steps before any simulation.

blocks.text: The Practice track follows the classic lysozyme-in-water tutorial. Before simulating, you build the system step by step. Each step reads the previous step's output.

flags: gmx pdb2gmx -f clean.pdb -o processed.gro -water spce -ff amber99sb-ildn
Builds the topology (topol.top) with a force field and water model, adds hydrogens. Remove crystal waters (HOH) first
Centers the protein (-c) in a cubic box (-bt) with 1.0 nm to each edge (-d)
gmx solvate -cp newbox.gro -cs spc216.gro -o solv.gro -p topol.top
Fills the box with water and adds the water count to topol.top
gmx grompp -f ions.mdp -c solv.gro -p topol.top -o ions.tpr
Combines everything into a .tpr; checks that coordinates and topology agree
echo SOL | gmx genion -s ions.tpr -o solv_ions.gro -p topol.top -pname NA -nname CL -neutral
Swaps some waters for Na+ and Cl- so the system's net charge is zero

blocks.text: The `[ molecules ]` section at the end of topol.top must list exactly what's in the coordinate file, in the same order. If you run solvate twice, or edit by hand, they disagree and grompp stops with "number of coordinates in coordinate file does not match topology".

try.text: Check the molecule counts at the end of `topol.top`.

blocks.warn: Some gmx programs ask you to pick a group from a menu (genion asks which group to replace with ions). In a script nobody can answer, so pipe the answer in: `echo SOL | gmx genion ...`.

quiz.q: grompp warns the system has a net charge of +8. What's the next step?
quiz.why: A charged system causes artifacts with PME electrostatics. genion -neutral adds 8 Cl- ions to balance it.

lessons.title: Minimizing, simulating and continuing
lessons.summary: mdrun, checking energies, GPUs, and checkpoints.

blocks.text: First, energy minimization relaxes clashes from building the system. Then, in the full protocol, come short equilibrations (NVT, then NPT) and the production run. Each step is grompp (make a .tpr) then mdrun (run it).

flags: gmx grompp -f minim.mdp -c solv_ions.gro -p topol.top -o em.tpr
-deffnm em names every output em.*; -v prints progress
Compute non-bonded forces on the GPU. Needs a GPU in the job, or mdrun stops
Pick up from the checkpoint after a TIMEOUT
echo Potential | gmx energy -f em.edr -o potential.xvg
Extract the potential energy over time

blocks.text: A good minimization ends with a large negative potential energy (around -5×10^5 kJ/mol for solvated lysozyme) and a maximum force below the target in minim.mdp.

example.out:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=md
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --time=1-00:00:00

module load gromacs
gmx mdrun -deffnm md -nb gpu -cpi md.cpt
example.note: -cpi continues from md.cpt if it exists and starts fresh if not, so the same script can be resubmitted after a TIMEOUT.

blocks.tip: GROMACS backs up instead of overwriting: rerun a step and the old file is renamed `#em.gro.1#`. Clean them up with `rm \#*`.

quiz.q: Your 24-hour MD job ends with TIMEOUT halfway through. What's the quickest fix?
options: Resubmit with gmx mdrun ... -cpi md.cpt to continue
quiz.why: mdrun writes checkpoints as it goes. -cpi continues from the last one instead of starting over.
